commands.response: `ls` — lists files in the current directory. Use `ls -la` for details including hidden files.
`cd <folder>` — changes directory. `cd ..` goes up one level. `cd ~` goes to home.
`mkdir <name>` — creates a new folder. Use `mkdir -p a/b/c` to create nested folders.
`rm <file>` — deletes a file. `rm -r <folder>` deletes a folder recursively. BE CAREFUL — no undo.
`git init` — initializes a new Git repo in the current directory.
`git add .` — stages all changes. `git add <file>` stages a specific file.
`git commit -m "message"` — commits staged changes with a message.
`git push origin main` — pushes commits to the remote repo.
After pushing, copy the mj script to your bin: `cp ~/github-projects/Mj.ai/mj ~/bin/mj`
`git clone <url>` — clones a remote repo to your local machine.
`git status` — shows changed, staged, and untracked files.
`npm install` — installs all packages listed in package.json. Use `npm install <pkg>` for a specific package.
Permission denied usually means you need `sudo` before the command, or the file/folder ownership is wrong. Try `sudo <command>` or `chmod +x <file>` if it's an executable.
'Command not found' means the program isn't installed or isn't in your PATH. Try installing it with `apt install <name>` (Debian/Ubuntu) or `pkg install <name>` (Termux).
The file or directory doesn't exist at that path. Check spelling, use `ls` to see what's there, and confirm you're in the right directory with `pwd`.
`cp <source> <destination>` — copies a file. `cp -r <folder> <destination>` copies a folder recursively. Example: `cp file.txt backup/file.txt`.
`sed -i 's/old/new/g' file.txt` — replaces all occurrences of 'old' with 'new' in file.txt in-place.
`cat <file>` — prints file contents to the terminal.
`pwd` — prints the full path of your current directory.
`mv` — moves or renames files and folders. Rename with `mv old.txt new.txt`, or move with `mv file.txt ~/Documents/`.
`less` — view a file one screen at a time. Run `less big.log`, scroll with arrows, search with `/word`, quit with `q`.
`head` — prints the first lines of a file. `head -n 20 log.txt` shows the first 20 lines (default 10).
`tail` — prints the last lines of a file. `tail -n 50 log.txt` for the last 50, or `tail -f log.txt` to follow it live.
`grep` — searches text for a pattern. `grep -rn "TODO" .` recursively shows matching lines with line numbers; add `-i` to ignore case.
`find` — searches the file tree by name, type, or age. `find . -name "*.js"` finds all .js files; add `-type f` to limit to files.
`chmod` — changes file permissions. `chmod +x script.sh` makes it runnable; `chmod 644 file` sets read/write owner, read-only others.
`chown` — changes a file's owner/group. `sudo chown user:group file.txt`; add `-R` to apply recursively to a folder.
`ps` — lists running processes. `ps aux` shows every process with CPU/memory; pipe to grep like `ps aux | grep node`.
`kill` — sends a signal to a process by PID. `kill 1234` asks it to quit; `kill -9 1234` forces it. Use `pkill name` to kill by name.
`top` — live view of processes by CPU/memory use. Press `q` to quit. `htop` is a friendlier color version if installed.
`df` — shows free space on mounted disks. `df -h` prints human-readable sizes like `12G` instead of raw blocks.
`du` — measures folder/file sizes. `du -sh *` shows a one-line total for each item in the current directory.
`tar` — bundles files into one archive. `tar -czf out.tar.gz folder/` creates a gzipped archive; `tar -xzf out.tar.gz` extracts it.
`gzip` — compresses a single file in place. `gzip big.log` makes `big.log.gz`; `gunzip big.log.gz` (or `gzip -d`) restores it.
`curl` — transfers data over HTTP and other protocols. `curl https://example.com` prints a page; `curl -O url` saves to a file.
`wget` — downloads files from the web. `wget https://site/file.zip` saves it locally; add `-c` to resume an interrupted download.
`ssh` — opens a secure shell on a remote machine. `ssh user@host` logs in; add `-p 2222` for a non-standard port.
`scp` — copies files over SSH. `scp file.txt user@host:/path/` uploads; reverse the args to download. Add `-r` for folders.
